extracted.intended_audience: state and local government officials, independent auditors, and federal cognizant audit agency personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on conducting and reporting organization-wide ('single') audits under Attachment P to OMB Circular A-102, including scope, objectives, sampling/materiality, subrecipient monitoring, audit reporting, cognizant agency roles, cost reimbursement, and sanctions. Intended to help grantees and auditors meet the Circular's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for organization-wide audit (frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular promulgates audit requirements for State and local governments to ensure that organization-wide audits usually will be made annually, but not less frequently than every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments and agencies administering programs involving grants must issue regulations to implement the Circular; when incorporated into grant agreements, the audit provisions are binding. (Q1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the single audit
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the organization-wide audit are to determine whether the organization's financial statements are reliable, its control systems are free of material weaknesses, and there is no indication of extensive noncompliance with applicable laws, regulations, and agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This objective differs from individual grant audits which focused primarily on grant-level compliance and questioned costs; the single audit provides Federal agencies with an indication of whether further auditing is warranted. (Q2)

rubrics_metrics.name: How single audit streamlines audit coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace numerous individual grant audits and duplicative coverage with one single, organization-wide audit, and standardize differing auditing approaches and reporting procedures prescribed by various Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single audit also eliminates gaps in audit coverage of Federal funds. (Q3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the organization (audit scope unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization should be the entity for which the government traditionally prepares financial statements (including grant financial statements) and obtains an audit; it may be the entire State or city or a department or other entity within a State or city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on what constitutes the organization should be made by State or local government officials, not by the Federal Government. (Q4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of all Federal funds and program types
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization-wide audit should cover all activities of the recipient organization that receive Federal funds; all Federal funds will be subject to audit whether or not the particular type of program is covered by other provisions of Circular A-102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes contracts, loans, loan guarantees, insurance programs and general revenue sharing funds as well as grants. (Q5)

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit period coverage (biennial audits and start dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient elects an audit every two years, the next audit should cover all transactions since the last audit; the period audited should relate to the auditee's fiscal year, not the grantor's fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no previous single audit exists, the auditor, recipient and cognizant audit agency should agree on a starting date; if beginning balances were not audited, note this in the report. (Q6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to block grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Omnibus Reconciliation Act requires State financial and compliance audits of block grant funds, there is no specific requirement that single audits be used; however, fulfilling block grant audit requirements via a single audit would conform with the legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present plans call for including major compliance requirements of block grant programs in the Approved Compliance Supplement. (Q7, Q10)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Approved Compliance Supplement for major programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 60 programs in the Compliance Supplement (representing over 90% of Federal aid to State and local governments), the audit of the compliance requirements contained in the supplement will meet the requirements of Attachment P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these programs it is not necessary for the auditor to review the applicable laws and regulations for additional compliance requirements; auditor should still review the award for special conditions. (Q8)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining compliance requirements for programs not in the supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal awards are subject to financial and compliance audit; for programs not in the Approved Compliance Supplement, the auditor should determine major compliance requirements from the award document, the Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance, and applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent practicable, these requirements should be verified with the cognizant audit agency. The auditor is not required to test every single award but must establish major requirements for selected audits. (Q9)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling preference and projection guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Either a nonstatistical or statistical approach to audit sampling may be used; statistical sampling is the preferred approach whenever the universe is susceptible to statistical treatment and the use of the technique is economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines do not, at this time, contain a requirement for projecting questioned costs to the universe. Agencies should rely on GAO guidelines and governmental audit standards. (Q12)

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality tests (application to financial statements and awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment P requires the materiality test be applied to general purpose financial statements or awards tested; amounts immaterial to financial statements might be material when related to awards tested because of stewardship responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors should recognize the stewardship aspect in government audits and apply materiality accordingly. (Q13)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient audit responsibilities of the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular requires the recipient to ensure that subrecipients have an audit made in accordance with Attachment P; the recipient must establish a system to assure subrecipient audits meet Attachment P and a follow-up system for questioned costs, internal control weaknesses and other exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient's auditor should review the recipient's system for obtaining and acting on subgrantee audit reports, test whether the system functions per procedures, and comment on monitoring and disbursing procedures as warranted. If subrecipient audits are not made and amounts are material, expand the recipient audit scope or note in the report that subrecipient charges were not tested. (Q14)

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit treatment of contracts and commercial contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit provisions of Circular A-102 do not apply to commercial contractors; State and local governments should use their own procedures to decide when and how to audit commercial contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should apply their normal contract audit policies for commercial contractors rather than Attachment P. (Q15)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and review of subrecipient audit reports by cognizant agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 15 required recipients to submit subrecipient audit reports to the cognizant audit agency, but this has proved impractical; in the meantime, grantees must review subgrantee reports and take appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change to the Circular will reflect impracticality; see answer to Q14 for expected recipient responsibilities. (Q16)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required audit report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular requires a report containing an opinion on financial statements and comments on compliance and weaknesses in and noncompliance with systems of internal control; such comments may be included in the audit report or a separate management letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management letters should be available to State, local and Federal officials. Audit reports must identify programs under which the organization received Federal funds and amounts of awards received; level of detail for individual grants may vary but meet at least minimum Circular requirements. (Q17, Q19, Q23)

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements to be audited (what must be prepared)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular does not require preparation of general purpose financial statements; it requires audit of those financial statements prepared by the recipient to meet its needs and the needs of other statement users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statements are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, the audit report should state the nature of the variances. Illustrative statements in GAO guidelines are illustrative only; auditors have shown summary data on grant activity in many reports. (Q17, Q18)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on internal accounting control (single report approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment P calls for comments on material weaknesses in and noncompliance with systems of internal control noted while studying and evaluating the system as part of the audit; it does not call for two reports on internal control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference GAO standards and AICPA SAS No. 30 for guidance on reporting on internal accounting control. (Q20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of accuracy and completeness of Federal financial reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment P calls for the auditor to comment on the accuracy and completeness of financial reports made to the Federal Government, but does not require a 100 percent audit of all reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors may determine accuracy and completeness through a review of internal systems used to accumulate data and tests of sample reports. (Q21)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizant audit agency roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognizant audit agencies are assigned to perform technical advice and liaison, desk reviews of audit reports, reviews of audit organizations and their work, addressing deficiencies noted during reviews, and processing audit reports by Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB is assigning cognizant agencies for the largest governments; for others, the Federal agency with the largest assistance funds will assume cognizant responsibilities. This booklet also answers many questions posed by cognizant agency personnel. (Q30, Q31)

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of audit scope/plan and auditor selection
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement for the Federal cognizant audit agency to approve the audit scope or plan in advance, nor to approve the auditor in advance; selection of an independent auditor is a grantee responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance approval is often useful to avoid conflicts; grantees selecting auditors should follow Procurement Standards in Attachment O to obtain services efficiently and economically with maximum open competition. (Q32, Q33)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of internal auditors' work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work performed by internal auditors should be a factor in determining the nature, timing and extent of independent auditor's procedures; the independent auditor should consider the competence and objectives of internal auditors and evaluate their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal auditors' work should be used to the maximum extent practicable in accordance with AICPA SAS No. 9. (Q24)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost impact and reimbursement for single audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Single audits may require up to about 20 percent more time than audits with only financial objectives, but total cost to an organization could be less than aggregate costs of numerous individual grant audits due to elimination of duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and local governments should use normal financing procedures to pay for single audits; Federal Government will reimburse grantees for its fair share of audit costs under Circular A-87, usually as part of allocated grant program costs. Alternate methods for payment are being considered for programs that don't allow indirect costs. (Q25, Q26, Q27)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial actions for noncompliance with Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: If grantees do not comply with Circular A-102 provisions, repayment of Federal funds is an option (usually last resort); other remedies include reduced indirect cost rates for future grants or withholding funds until the audit is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies may impose remedies depending on circumstances. (Q28)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions triggering additional Federal audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies may perform additional audits after a single audit if independent auditor found significant internal control weaknesses, to follow up on common program problems, when audit coverage is insufficient, to investigate allegations of fraud/waste/abuse, or to conduct economy/efficiency/program results audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachment P does not limit Federal authority to perform further audits; additional work should be based upon work already performed. (Q29)

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations regarding small and minority audit firms (Paragraph 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of Federal funds must provide the maximum practicable opportunity for small audit firms and firms owned/controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals to be considered for selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement establishes a fair and open selection process but does not require selection of particular firms or classes of firms; cognizant agencies do not have authority to challenge a recipient's choice of audit firm. (Q34)

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical considerations and updates to Attachment P
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to Attachment P will be made when experience or feedback indicates need; the Director of OMB will solicit views of Federal agencies, State/local officials, professional organizations and others before important changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB will use suggestions in interpreting or revising requirements; some provisions (e.g., submission of subrecipient reports) may be revised as impracticalities are identified. (Q38, Q16)
